11395/14.question: which operand chooses the arm this form returns
11395/14.verdict: OPERAND 2 CARRIES THE SELECTION. Holding both value operands distinct on every case and writing operand 2 with `imms`, the returned arm changes on 4 of 8 cases between operand 2 = 0 and = 1 - and on those cases the two sweeps return the OPPOSITE arms, which a constant or a move cannot do. This is the same carrier as `11375/14 select`, whose operand 2 is 1 for `>`/`>=` and 0 for `<`/`<=`. Operand 2 = 2 and = 3 would not ENCODE (T11395.cond2, T11395.cond3), so the field is one bit wide. What is NOT settled is which relation each value names: a select cannot separate `>` from `>=` structurally, and the library holds no three-operand select of this shape - GPR16 predicate source with two GPR32 arms - so the exact-match census still reports no candidate.

1287/10.question: is its sixteen-bit source a half or a bfloat
1287/10.verdict: the source is a BFLOAT16: 16 of 16 cases match the bfloat column and 0 match the half column, with 16 distinct outputs - so no constant could have produced this agreement. The first attempt at this batch chose cases on which the bfloat column was the single value 0x3F80, and a constant output matched it perfectly while identifying nothing.

3290/6.question: does the six-byte form share the flushing NaN convention of the fourteen-byte one
3290/6.verdict: NOT ANSWERED, and the reason is a capability rather than a result. The field map authored FOURTEEN bytes for this opcode on both attempts - sixteen cases, then six chosen to match the shape of the existing six-byte record - so the dispatch determined `3290/14` again and said nothing about `3290/6`. A form is (opcode, width). The six-byte encoding has to be supplied as bytes.
